_README: #5072 (epic #5067): the panel rubric — a FIXED standard the training plan is graded against, one seat per school of the training charter's concession_ledger (the seat keys must equal the ledger's keys; tests/test_panel_rubric_5072.py holds it). Each criterion is graded by CODE (a named check in lambdas/training/panel_rubric.py CHECKS, ADR-105: deterministic computation before any model verdict) or by the JUDGE (lambdas/training/panel_judge.py, route charter.judge / charter.judge_gate) when code cannot check it. The concession each seat makes is READ from the charter at grade time, never copied here. The target (overall letter, every-seat floor) is the charter's panel_target. Hand-owned; a change is a new version with a change_log line.

change_log.what: the eight seats, 40 criteria (32 by code, 8 by the judge), the letter scale

food_panel: nine nutrition seats (six schools, three roles) from the charter's nutrition.concession_ledger, 45 criteria (36 by code against the resolved food plan, 9 by the judge), graded on the same letter scale and the same panel_target; built on the panel defaults, pending R1 and R2 (#5091)

food_panel energy rows (owner ruling 2026-10-23, #5091 follow-up 3: 'Food-plan grader: energy rows grade against the 1,500 target. The 1,600/1,800 lines show as warnings, not failures'): day_floors_held and week_mean_floor grade against the day's target and the week's mean target while the charter's nutrition.calories.floor_role is warning, the floor gaps shown as warnings in the evidence; week_balanced grades the no-payback training-day rule (follow-up 2: lifting days +150, rest days not paid back below the target)

overall_rule: the overall score is the mean of the eight seat scores, mapped through `letters`; a seat score is the mean of its criteria; the target is met only when the overall letter reaches the charter's panel_target.overall AND every seat reaches panel_target.every_seat_at_least

calibration.rule: the judge is uncalibrated until the owner has graded this many plans by hand and the judge's seat scores sit within 1 point of his on each; every grade carries its calibration state

food_panel._README: #5110 (epic #5094): the FOOD panel — the same harness grading the week's food plan, one seat per school or role of the charter's nutrition.concession_ledger (the seat keys must equal the ledger's keys; tests/test_food_panel_5110.py holds it). A CODE criterion names a check in lambdas/training/food_panel.py CHECKS, read from the food plan the platform resolves (health.calorie_target.resolve per day, the protein engine's range and feedings, the macro floors, the week's titration record); a JUDGE criterion is graded by the same blinded judge (training/panel_judge.py) on the same routes. Seats name schools and roles, never people: issue #5110 names six schools by their leading figure and each gets its own seat (the person-to-seat map is on PR #5206), plus the three roles. The bar is the charter's panel_target, the letters above. Built on the panel defaults R1 (eat up to the band, weekly refit) and R2 (the range in four feedings), pending the owner (#5091).
food_panel.plan_shape: lambdas/training/food_panel.py build_food_plan: {case_id, panel: food, week_start, charter_version, days: [7 x the resolver's day (date, day_type, kcal, base_kcal, uplift_kcal, band, floors, source, provenance, balance_held, split, pre_post_session) + the day's intended feedings], protein: the engine's range and feeding rule, floors: the macro floors, titration: the week's record or null}

calibration.rule: the food judge is uncalibrated until the owner has graded this many real food plans by hand and the judge's seat scores sit within 1 point of his on each
